A.explanation: X has a net $20 \text{ N}$ to the left and the $20 \text{ N}$ equal-opposite part forms a clockwise couple of $20 \times 0.50 = 10 \text{ N m}$.

B.explanation: X is not a pure couple because $20 \text{ N}$ and $40 \text{ N}$ do not cancel, so a net $20 \text{ N}$ force remains.

C.explanation: Y does have a net $20 \text{ N}$ to the left, but the equal $20 \text{ N}$ part gives only $20 \times 0.50 = 10 \text{ N m}$, not $30 \text{ N m}$.

D.explanation: Y is not a pure couple because $40 \text{ N}$ and $20 \text{ N}$ do not cancel, and its couple part is $10 \text{ N m}$, not $30 \text{ N m}$.

hints: Notice the sizes and directions in X: $20 \text{ N}$ to the right on top and $40 \text{ N}$ to the left below, $50 \text{ cm}$ apart, so they cannot cancel to zero force.
Split an unequal opposite pair into an equal opposite couple plus the leftover force: for X think $20 \text{ N}$ versus $20 \text{ N}$ plus an extra $20 \text{ N}$ to the left.
Calculate a couple torque with $\text{torque} = F \times d$ using $d = 0.50 \text{ m}$ and decide clockwise versus anticlockwise from which way the top moves and the bottom moves.
walkthrough: Convert the separation to metres: $50 \text{ cm} = 0.50 \text{ m}$ for both X and Y, since torque must be in $\text{N m}$.
Find the vector resultant force for X: $+20 \text{ N}$ right and $-40 \text{ N}$ right gives $-20 \text{ N}$, i.e. $20 \text{ N}$ to the left, so X cannot be a torque only.
Split X into a balanced part and a leftover: $20 \text{ N}$ right on top with $20 \text{ N}$ left below is a couple, leaving an extra $20 \text{ N}$ to the left.
Calculate that couple torque: $T = Fd = 20 \times 0.50 = 10 \text{ N m}$. Top to the right and bottom to the left turns the system clockwise.

Check Y the same way: $40 \text{ N}$ left and $20 \text{ N}$ right gives $20 \text{ N}$ left resultant, and the $20 \text{ N}$ balanced part gives $20 \times 0.50 = 10 \text{ N m}$ anticlockwise, so $30 \text{ N m}$ is wrong.
Therefore X is a $10 \text{ N m}$ clockwise torque plus a $20 \text{ N}$ force to the left. This is option A.
